Blandish

BLAN-dish · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To blandish to charm someone with flattery or kind words.

Diplomats sometimes blandish a difficult foreign minister before raising the harder topics.

Worked Example

The car salesman tried to blandish the couple with compliments about their taste before mentioning the price.

Complimenting a couple's taste right before the price talk is exactly blandishing.

How Blandish Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

flatter

flatter: praise excessively to please or persuade

sweet-talk: win over with flattering words

Antonyms

browbeat

browbeat: pressure someone with harsh words

How Strong Is It? — compliment → butter up → blandish

compliment vs. blandish

compliment vs. blandish: A compliment is a single, often sincere kind remark; blandish implies a intentional STRATEGY of flattery aimed at getting something in return.

butter up vs. blandish

butter up vs. blandish: To butter someone up is the same idea in casual slang, while blandish is the more formal, literary word for exactly that tactic.

Put it together

Put it together: Blandish comes from Latin blandus ('smooth, flattering') + -ire -- literally 'to make smooth,' i.e. to smooth someone over with flattery.

Use the root in a new word: bland

Use the root in a new word: bland: The same blandus root gives us the everyday word bland -- both trace back to something 'smooth,' whether smooth-tasting food or smooth-talking flattery.
